title: Immortal Sacrifice!
transcript: Can you imagine the euphoria of beating the best chess player of all time with an incredible queen sacrifice? Well, Brazilian Grandmaster Luis Paoui can. This position is from a blitz game between Magnus Carlson playing as black and Luis Paoui playing as white. In this position, Grandmaster Supi prepared a battery with rook to A2. He's preparing to bring the other rook on the A file and attack the king. Magnus knew that he was worse in this position, but he tried to win the bishop by attacking it twice with the bishop and queen. If white had tried to save the bishop by taking the black bishop, now after queen takes F3, G takes F3 and recapturing the bishop, black is actually winning, having an extra knight. Instead, Grandmaster Sup ignores the threat on the bishop and plays rook F A1. Of course, the bishop cannot be taken because this is a checkmate threat. So Magnus moved his king to C8 and now he was looking to escape via D7. And it seems like white's attack has run out of steam. If you simply check the king, the king is going to run out and there's no checkmate. But Subie had seen the beautiful and incredible queen C6, giving up the queen [music] completely just to cover the D7 square. Now you have to take the queen because otherwise rook to A8 is going to be checkmate. The king cannot run out. But once you do, the pawn is going to capture back. And this is still a brilliant move because you're technically sacrificing the bishop. All of the escape squares of the king are covered. And there is no way to stop the rook from coming to A8. And this was the reaction of Magnus Carlson to this move. That is dirty. Wow. Wow. If you want to be able to find moves like this, I suggest you check out my friends at Chess Mind AI. Their app uses a modern and smart approach to chess improvement.
